note: CAC-RW-1.9. Publications that must not be cited as current. The complement to sources.json: that file watches what a skill DOES cite, and structurally cannot see a withdrawn publication the skill does not cite yet. This one guards the citation that has not been written. A designation here may still appear in prose that DISCUSSES its withdrawal — the check requires a withdrawal marker nearby, not silence.

entries.label: SP 800-61, Rev. 1 and Rev. 2 (Computer Security Incident Handling Guide)
entries.supersededBy: SP 800-61 Rev. 3, Incident Response Recommendations and Considerations for Cybersecurity Risk Management: A CSF 2.0 Community Profile — Final, 3 April 2025
entries.why: The single most-quoted structure in incident response is r2's four-phase lifecycle, and essentially every secondary source still repeats it. r3 is a CSF 2.0 Community Profile and is organised differently. This is the entry the whole list was created for.

entries.label: SP 800-171 Rev. 1 and Rev. 2
entries.why: The trap runs BOTH directions. Rev. 2 is withdrawn by NIST and still contractually live under DFARS clauses that name it by revision. Never cite it as current NIST guidance; never tell a defense contractor it is irrelevant to them either. Say which of the two you mean.

entries.label: SP 800-50 (2003), Building an Information Technology Security Awareness and Training Program
entries.supersededBy: SP 800-50 Rev. 1, Building a Cybersecurity and Privacy Learning Program — Final, 12 September 2024
entries.why: The retitle matters: 'awareness and training' became 'learning program', and citing the old title signals the old model.

entries.label: NIST IR 8374 (2022), Ransomware Risk Management: A Cybersecurity Framework Profile
entries.supersededBy: NIST IR 8374 Rev. 1, Ransomware Risk Management: A Cybersecurity Framework 2.0 Community Profile — Final, 11 June 2026
entries.why: The original profiles CSF 1.1. Rev. 1 profiles CSF 2.0, which is the framework this suite assesses against.

entries.label: SP 800-53A, Rev. 1 and Rev. 4
entries.why: Easy to confuse with SP 800-53 Rev. 5, the controls catalogue, which patches on its own schedule. 800-53A is the assessment guide and its Rev. 5 has been final since January 2022. A seed list for this file had the two conflated.

entries.label: SP 800-18 Rev. 1 (2006)
entries.supersededBy: SP 800-18 Rev. 2, Developing Security, Privacy, and Cybersecurity Supply Chain Risk Management Plans for Systems — Final, 30 June 2026
entries.why: Rev. 2 is final, so Rev. 1 is superseded. Listed as `superseded` rather than `withdrawn` because Rev. 1's own CSRC status was not confirmed in the pass that authored this row — the distinction is kept rather than guessed.

notYetVerified.note: Candidates from the seed list that this pass could NOT confirm against CSRC, and which are therefore NOT enforced. Listing them is the point: an unverified ban is as bad as an unverified citation.
candidates: SP 800-16 (1998) — did not surface in a CSRC search; status unconfirmed
CSF 1.1 — not in the SP series, so not in the CSRC publication catalogue; needs checking at nist.gov/cyberframework
SP 800-100 — the seed called its withdrawal record confusing. CSRC reports it FINAL (7 March 2007). An old final is not a withdrawn document, so it is deliberately absent from `entries`.
